The '''LAV 6''', sometimes written as '''LAV 6.0''' or '''LAV VI''', is the fourth generation of the [[LAV (Canada)|Light Armoured Vehicle (LAV)]] family of [[armored personnel carrier]]s, and is based on the [[LAV III]]. The first LAV 6s were delivered in 2013 and entered service in 2016 following a period of testing.<ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 20" /><ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 22" /><ref name="Canada.ca LAVUP" /> The Canadian Army plans to replace its entire LAV fleet of various [[LAV II]] and LAV III variants with the LAV 6. The vehicle is being acquired in two main variants: a fighting vehicle equipped with the 25mm cannon seen on the LAV II and LAV III, and a support variant labelled the Armoured Combat Support Vehicle (ACSV).

==History==
In July 2009, the [[Department of National Defence (Canada)|Canadian Department of National Defence]] announced that $5 billion would be spent to enhance, replace and repair the [[Canadian Army]]'s armoured vehicles. Part of the spending would be used to replace and repair damaged LAV III's due to wear and tear from [[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|operations in Afghanistan]]. As many as one third of the Army's light armoured vehicles were out of service.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/top-soldier-says-afghan-action-wearing-out-equipment-1.378073|title=LAV-III out of service|publisher=CTV|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090710091526/http://www.ctv.ca/servlet/ArticleNews/print/CTVNews/20090310/afghanistan_break_090310/20090310/?hub=SEAfghanistan&subhub=PrintStory|archive-date=July 10, 2009|df=mdy-all}}</ref> The LAV III's would be upgraded with improved protection and automotive components.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://ottawacitizen.com/news/todays-paper/Somnia/1653152/story.html |newspaper=Ottawa Citizen |first1=David |last1=Pugliese |title=Military wants $5B for army's fleet |date=June 2, 2009}} {{dead link |date=March 2016 |fix-attempted=yes}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

The Canadian Army lost over 34 vehicles and 359 were damaged during the mission in Afghanistan. The Canadian Army lost 13 LAVs and more than 159 were damaged by roadside bombs or enemy fire.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://o.canada.com/2012/07/19/78433/|title=Canadian military lost 34 vehicles in Afghanistan, 359 damaged|publisher=Canada.ca|date=July 20, 2012|access-date=July 20, 2012|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120720203223/http://o.canada.com/2012/07/19/78433/|archive-date=July 20, 2012|df=mdy-all}}</ref> Of the $5 billion announced, approximately 20% of it was intended to be used to upgrade LAV III models. The upgrade extended the LAV III life span to 2035. The remaining $4 billion was to be spent on a "new family of land combat vehicles".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/military-to-get-5b-for-armoured-vehicles-1.864104|title=Military to get $5B for armoured vehicles|publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation]]|date=July 7, 2009|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090708191354/http://www.cbc.ca/canada/story/2009/07/07/nb-military-funding-432.html|archive-date=July 8, 2009|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

The Department of National Defence considered the purchase of a Close Combat Vehicle, meant to accompany the [[Leopard 2]] and to support the LAV III in combat. The [[Combat Vehicle 90|CV90]], the [[Puma (IFV)]] and the [[Véhicule blindé de combat d'infanterie]] were the most likely candidates for the role. A contract of 108 with an option for up to 30 more was considered.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.forces.gc.ca/site/news-nouvelles/view-news-afficher-nouvelles-eng.asp?id=3036|title=Close Combat Vehicle|date=July 8, 2009|access-date=November 11, 2009|publisher=[[Department of National Defence (Canada)|Department of National Defence]]|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090916213738/http://www.forces.gc.ca/site/news-nouvelles/view-news-afficher-nouvelles-eng.asp?id=3036|archive-date=September 16, 2009|df=mdy-all}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.defenseindustrydaily.com/Canada-Looks-to-Upgrade-Its-Armor-in-Afghanistan-05190/|title=Canada Looks to Upgrade Its Armor|date=July 9, 2009|access-date=November 11, 2009|publisher=Defense Industry Daily|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090712122949/http://www.defenseindustrydaily.com/Canada-Looks-to-Upgrade-Its-Armor-in-Afghanistan-05190/|archive-date=July 12, 2009|df=mdy-all}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://news.globaltv.com/story.html?id=2682413 |title=Plans for new fleet of armoured combat vehicles back on track |author=David Pugliese |date=January 21, 2010 |publisher=[[Global News]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110711101811/http://news.globaltv.com/story.html?id=2682413 |archive-date=July 11, 2011 |df=mdy-all }}</ref> The success of the upgrade program and budget pressures led to the cancellation of the Close Combat Vehicle replacement program.<ref>{{cite web |date=December 23, 2013 |title=Canada cancels $2.1B armored vehicle purchase |url=http://www.defensenews.com/article/20131223/DEFREG02/312230002 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20131223155555/http://www.defensenews.com/article/20131223/DEFREG02/312230002 |archive-date=December 23, 2013 |access-date=December 23, 2013 |website=defensenews.com |publisher=AGENCE FRANCE-PRESSE}}</ref>

In October 2011, the Canadian government announced a $1.1 billion contract to General Dynamics Land Systems to upgrade 550 LAV III combat vehicles. The government said the upgrade was needed to improve protection against mines and improvised explosive devices (IEDs), which have been the cause of a number of Canadian deaths in Afghanistan. The improvements will also extend the service of the vehicles up to 2035 and will boost troop mobility.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.radio-canada.ca/regions/alberta/2011/10/21/002-contrat-edmonton-modernisation-vehicules-forces-canadienne.shtml|title=Un milliard $ pour moderniser la flotte de véhicules blindés des Forces canadiennes|date=October 21, 2011|publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation|Radio-Canada]]|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111023035702/http://www.radio-canada.ca/regions/alberta/2011/10/21/002-contrat-edmonton-modernisation-vehicules-forces-canadienne.shtml|archive-date=October 23, 2011|df=mdy-all}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://fr.canoe.com/infos/quebeccanada/politiquefederale/archives/2011/10/20111021-143706.html|title=1 milliard $ pour moderniser des véhicules blindés|date=October 21, 2011|publisher=[[Agence QMI]]|access-date=October 22, 2011}}{{dead link|date=April 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.ledevoir.com/politique/canada/334284/ottawa-investit-un-milliard-pour-les-blindes-legers-canadiens |title=Ottawa investit un milliard pour les blindés légers canadiens |date=October 21, 2011 |publisher=[[Le Devoir]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131224112211/http://www.ledevoir.com/politique/canada/334284/ottawa-investit-un-milliard-pour-les-blindes-legers-canadiens |archive-date=December 24, 2013 |df=mdy-all }}</ref>

The upgrades include a new and more powerful [[engine]], increased armour protection, and improved steering and brake systems. The turret hatches on the LAV III would be made larger and fire control, thermal, day and low-light sights, and data displays would be improved. The weight of the vehicle would increase from {{convert|38000|lb|kg}} to {{convert|55000|lb|kg}}.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.defensenews.com/story.php?i=7120066|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120729182105/http://www.defensenews.com/story.php?i=7120066|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 29, 2012|title=LAV-3 Upgrade Still a Priority for Canada|date=October 21, 2011 |publisher=[[Defense News]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://blogs.ottawacitizen.com/2011/10/21/government-makes-it-official-general-dynamics-land-systems-awarded-lav-3-upgrade-contract/|title=Government Makes It Official: General Dynamics Land Systems Awarded LAV-3 Upgrade Contract|date=October 21, 2011|publisher=[[Ottawa Citizen]]|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111228135045/http://blogs.ottawacitizen.com/2011/10/21/government-makes-it-official-general-dynamics-land-systems-awarded-lav-3-upgrade-contract/|archive-date=December 28, 2011|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

In September 2012, the original contract valued at $1.064 billion to upgrade the 550 LAV III variants (infantry section carrier, command post, [[observation post]] and engineer vehicle) to the LAV 6 configuration was modified. The modification added $151 million to upgrade an additional 66 LAV III's to the LAV 6 with a LAV Reconnaissance and Surveillance System (LRSS) fitted.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.vanguardcanada.com/2014/01/29/lav-6-0-protected-mobile-lethal/ |title=LAV 6.0: Protected, mobile and lethal |date=January 29, 2014 |website=vanguardcanada.com |publisher=Deanna R |access-date=April 22, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170424000505/http://www.vanguardcanada.com/2014/01/29/lav-6-0-protected-mobile-lethal/ |archive-date=April 24, 2017 |df=mdy-all }}</ref>

In February 2017, GDLS – Canada was awarded a $404 million order to work on 141 LAV Operational Requirement Integration Task (LORIT) vehicles. This contract will upgrade the remaining LAV III fleet in the Canadian Army to the LAV 6 configuration. This brings the Canadian Army's LAV III Upgrade (LAVUP) program to a total cost of $1.8 billion.<ref name="ottawacitizen.com">{{cite web|url=https://ottawacitizen.com/news/national/defence-watch/defence-minister-sajjan-to-make-announcement-on-lav-iii-upgrade-project|title=Defence Minister Sajjan to make announcement on LAV-III Upgrade project|date=February 9, 2017|website=Ottawa Citizen|access-date=May 3, 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170729004603/http://ottawacitizen.com/news/national/defence-watch/defence-minister-sajjan-to-make-announcement-on-lav-iii-upgrade-project|archive-date=July 29, 2017|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

Final completion and delivery of the Canadian Army's LAV III Upgrade (LAVUP) to upgrade the LAV III to the LAV 6 was expected to be completed by December 2019.<ref name="janes.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.janes.com/article/67691/canada-to-modernise-additional-141-lav-iiis|title=Canada to modernise additional 141 LAV IIIs|website=janes.com|access-date=May 3, 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170217040239/http://www.janes.com/article/67691/canada-to-modernise-additional-141-lav-iiis|archive-date=February 17, 2017|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

===Exports===
In early 2014 the [[Conservative Party of Canada|Conservative]] government under [[Stephen Harper]] prepared the sale of several hundred LAV 6 vehicles to Saudi Arabia for an estimated CAD $10 billion. This was one of the largest manufacturing export deals in modern Canadian history, though it was heavily criticized due to Saudi Arabia's record on human rights abuses and involving in the [[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2014/4/14/canada-saudi-arms-deal-has-significant-risk |title=Canada-Saudi arms deal has 'significant risk' |website=Al Jazeera |date=14 April 2014}}</ref> The deal, which grew to CAD $15 billion and included 928 LAV 6 vehicles, was ultimately signed in late 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/harper-defending-military-deal-with-saudi-arabia/article26550145/ |title=Harper defends military deal with Saudi Arabia |website=The Globe and Mail |date=25 September 2015}}</ref> The Liberal government under Justin Trudeau finally approved the export license for the vehicles after [[2015 Canadian federal election|coming to power]] in 2015, despite widespread calls from the [[New Democratic Party|NDP]] and human rights groups to cancel the deal. Even after footage appearing online of Canadian LAV vehicles being deployed against the Shiite population in Qatif, the House of Commons committee report found "no conclusive evidence that Canadian-made vehicles were used in human rights violations" according to Finance Minister [[Chrystia Freeland]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/saudi-lav-deal-1.4585035 |title=Trudeau defends Saudi arms export deal, points finger at Harper government |website=CBC News |date=20 September 2018}}</ref> The government also cited costly penalties for breaking the contract as a reason to honor the export commitments.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/trudeau-metro-morning-lavs-saudis-1.4874383 |title='Difficult contract' binds Canada to Saudi LAV deal, Trudeau says |website=CBC News |date=23 October 2018}}</ref> In 2018, Saudi Arabia threatened to reduce its order for LAV 6 vehicles from 928 to only 742 vehicles, after a diplomatic row with the Trudeau government following criticism of the former's human rights abuses, although some analysts believed this threat had more to do with the kingdom's economic difficulties.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/saudi-arabia-arms-canada-1.4815571 |title=Canada's arms deal with Saudi Arabia is shrinking |website=CBC News |date=10 September 2018}}</ref>

Following the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]], the Canadian Government announced that it would be diverting 39 LAV 6 ACSVs to the [[Ukrainian Armed Forces]] as [[military aid]] from the order of 360 vehicles it had previously made for the Canadian Army.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/nato-arms-canada-1.6506611 |title=Trudeau promises to arm Ukraine with modern military equipment |website=CBC News |date=30 June 2022}}</ref> Canadian officials stated that the vehicles along with spare parts would be delivered during the summer of 2022 and that the Army would still receive a total order of 360 vehicles in addition to the 39 vehicles given to Ukraine.<ref name="Ukraine ACSVs Global" >{{cite web|url=https://globalnews.ca/news/8958186/canada-military-aid-ukraine/ |title=As NATO summit ends, Canada promises more military aid to Ukraine |website=globalnews.ca |access-date=2022-06-30|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220630230815/https://globalnews.ca/news/8958186/canada-military-aid-ukraine/|archive-date=2022-06-30|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Ukraine ACSVs CBC" >{{cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/nato-arms-canada-1.6506611 |title=Trudeau promises to arm Ukraine with modern military equipment |website=www.cbc.ca |access-date=2022-06-30|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220630203815/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/nato-arms-canada-1.6506611|archive-date=2022-06-30|url-status=live}}</ref>

In July 2026, the Government of Canada announced the acquisition of a further 190 ACSVs from GDLS-Canada, which would bring the Canadian Army's total ACSV fleet to 550 vehicles.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-07-16 |title=Prime Minister Carney announces landmark partnership with General Dynamics Land Systems-Canada to build new fleet of armoured combat vehicles for the Canadian Armed Forces |url=https://www.pm.gc.ca/en/news/news-releases/2026/07/16/prime-minister-carney-announces-landmark-partnership-general-dynamics |access-date=2026-07-16 |website=Prime Minister of Canada |language=en}}</ref>

===Active combat===
In early January 2023 the first ACSVs were spotted near the frontlines in Ukraine, after having begun to arrive since early October 2022, with the vehicles previously having been in rear-area units for training on the vehicles.<ref name="ACSVs & Super Bison NP" /> Ukrainian Media reporting on the vehicles also dubbed the vehicles with a new nickname, the “Super Bison” due to the lineage the ACSV series shares with the older LAV 2 Bison series which filled an almost identical role.<ref name="ACSVs & Super Bison NP" >{{cite web|url=https://nationalpost.com/news/canada/made-in-canada-armoured-vehicles-ukraine |title=Fleets of made-in-Canada armoured vehicles start reaching Ukrainian battlefields |website=nationalpost.com |access-date=2023-01-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230123195834/https://nationalpost.com/news/canada/made-in-canada-armoured-vehicles-ukraine|archive-date=2023-01-23|url-status=live}}</ref> As of June 2025, two Super Bisons been confirmed by open source intelligence as destroyed in combat.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oryxspioenkop.com/2022/02/attack-on-europe-documenting-ukrainian.html  |title=Attack On Europe: Documenting Ukrainian Equipment Losses During The Russian Invasion Of Ukraine  |website=Oryx |access-date=2024-04-19}}</ref>

==Variants==

=== LAV 6 series ===
* '''LAV III UP''' (Upgraded) - The original prototype(s) that took the [[LAV III]] and modified it heavily under the Light armoured vehicle III upgrade (LAVUP) program into what eventually became the '''LAV 6 ISC'''.<ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 20" /><ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 22" /><ref name="Canada.ca LAVUP" />
* '''LAV 6 ISC''' (Infantry Section Carrier) - The basic IFV variant fitted with a turret and armed with a [[M242 Bushmaster]], a coaxial [[FN MAG|C6 GPMG]], and a roof mount for another C6 GPMG or [[FN Minimi|C9A2]].<ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 20" /><ref name="Canada.ca LAV 6" /><ref name="Canada.ca LAVUP">{{cite web |title=Light armoured vehicle III upgrade (LAVUP) |website=canada.ca |url=https://www.canada.ca/en/department-national-defence/services/procurement/light-armoured-vehicle-iii-upgrade.html |url-status=usurped |archive-date=2022-06-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220614123528/https://www.canada.ca/en/department-national-defence/services/procurement/light-armoured-vehicle-iii-upgrade.html}}</ref>
* '''LAV 6 CP''' (Command Post) - The mobile tactical command variant which lacks a turret and instead has a raised roofline on the rear half of the hull. Armed with a [[FN MAG|C6 GPMG]] on a RWS (Remote Weapon Station).<ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 20" /><ref name="Canada.ca LAV 6" /><ref name="Canada.ca LAVUP" />
* '''LAV 6 CE''' (Combat Engineering) - The engineering variant fitted with a hydraulic reel at the rear of the vehicle and a dozer blade at the front of the vehicle. It also lacks the turret of the ISC variant and is instead fitted occasionally with the RWS (Remote Weapon Station) armed with a [[FN MAG|C6 GPMG]].<ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 20" /><ref name="Canada.ca LAV 6" /><ref name="Canada.ca LAVUP" />
* '''LAV 6 Recce''' (Reconnaissance Vehicle) - A reconnaissance variant meant to partially replace the [[Bison and Coyote armoured vehicles|Coyote]] in the recce role. Unlike the '''OPV''' variant the vehicle is almost identical to the '''ISC''' variant, just with the addition of equipment for the recce role.<ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 20" /><ref name="Canada.ca LAV 6" /><ref name="Canada.ca LAVUP" />
* '''LAV 6 OPV''' (Observation Post Vehicle) - A forward observer/reconnaissance variant meant to partially replace the [[Bison and Coyote armoured vehicles|Coyote]] in the recce role. The vehicle is similar to the '''Recce''' variant but has a surveillance suite mounted on a retractable mast that can extend up to 5&nbsp;m when moving and 10&nbsp;m when stationary.<ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 20" /><ref name="Canada.ca LAV 6" /><ref name="Canada.ca LAVUP" />
* '''LAV 6 SHORAD''' (Short-Range Air Defence) - A concept vehicle designed to meet the Canadian Army's air defense requirement, first displayed at CANSEC defence exhibition in 2018. The vehicle is armed with a roof mounted SAM launcher with 3 tubes fitted to the left side of the vehicle, overtop of the troop compartment. The vehicle lacked any form of RWS (Remote Weapon Station) for protection.<ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 20" /><ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 22" />
* '''LAV 6 CRV''' (Combat Reconnaissance Vehicle) - A prototype vehicle designed for the Australian Army's Land 400 requirement for a wheeled combat reconnaissance vehicle. The vehicle is fitted with an unmanned MCT-30 turret and a [[CROWS]]. The vehicle was unsuccessful in the competition with the [[Boxer (armoured fighting vehicle)|Boxer CRV]] being chosen instead.<ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 20" /><ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 22" />

=== LAV 6 ACSV (Armoured Combat Support Vehicle) ===
This series was initially known as the LAV 6 CSV, and include the following variants:<ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 20" /><ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 22" /><ref name="LAV 6 GDLSC">{{cite web |title=LAV 6.0 Brochure |url=https://www.gdlscanada.com/products/LAV/LAV-6.0.html |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220924233313/https://www.gdlscanada.com/products/LAV/LAV-6.0.html |archive-date=2022-09-24 |website=gdlscanada.com}}</ref>
* '''ACSV TCV''' (Troop/Cargo Vehicle) - A basic APC variant that replaces the [[Bison and Coyote armoured vehicles|Bison]] as a general purpose armoured personnel carrier which can also double as a logistics carrier depending on operational requirements. The vehicle is fitted with a Protector RWS (Remote Weapon Station) armed with [[FN MAG|C6 GPMG]]; although it can also potentially mount a [[Heckler & Koch GMG|C16 CASW]] or a [[M2 Browning|M2HB QCB]].<ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 22" /><ref name="Canada.ca ACSV">{{cite web |title=Armoured Combat Support Vehicle (ACSV) |website=canada.ca |url=https://www.canada.ca/en/department-national-defence/services/procurement/armoured-combat-support-vehicle.html |url-status=usurped |archive-date=2022-08-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220817195750/https://www.canada.ca/en/department-national-defence/services/procurement/armoured-combat-support-vehicle.html}}</ref>
* '''ACSV AA''' (Armoured Ambulance) - A field ambulance variant meant for transporting wounded personnel, replacing the older [[Variants of the M113 armored personnel carrier#Canada|MTVA and M113A3 Ambulance]] along with the Bison Ambulance.<ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 22" /><ref name="Canada.ca ACSV" /><ref name="LAV 6 GDLSC" />
* '''ACSV CP''' (Command Post) - A command variant that replaces the older Bison CP and [[Variants of the M113 armored personnel carrier#Canada|M577A3 CP]] vehicles.<ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 20" /><ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 22" /><ref name="Canada.ca ACSV" />
* '''ACSV MRT''' (Mobile Repair Team) - Replacing the older [[Variants of the M113 armored personnel carrier#Canada|M113A3 MRT]], the vehicle is fitted with both a winch and a crane, which are used for repairing and assisting with the recovery of LAVs in the field.<ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 22" /><ref name="Canada.ca ACSV" />
* '''ACSV FCV''' (Fitter/Cargo Vehicle) - Replacing the older [[Variants of the M113 armored personnel carrier#Canada|MTVF]], the vehicle is fitted with a crane to repair vehicles in the field.<ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 22" /><ref name="Canada.ca ACSV" />
* '''ACSV EV''' (Engineering Vehicle) - An engineer variant that is fitted with a hydraulic dozer blade. This variant also replaces the older [[Variants of the M113 armored personnel carrier#Canada|MTVE]].<ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 22" /><ref name="Canada.ca ACSV" />
* '''ACSV EW''' (Electronic Warfare) - This variant is similar to the '''TCV''' variant but has an electronic warfare suite fitted in the rear of the vehicle. This vehicle replaces the Bisons that had been converted for electronic warfare.<ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 20" /><ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 22" /><ref name="Canada.ca ACSV" />
* '''ACSV MRV''' (Maintenance and Recovery Vehicle) - The recovery vehicle variant is fitted with a hydraulic dozer blade, a crane, two stabilizing support legs, and a Protector RWS (Remote Weapon Station) armed with [[FN MAG|C6 GPMG]]; although it can also potentially mount a [[Heckler & Koch GMG|C16 CASW]] or a [[M2 Browning|M2HB QCB]]. This variant replaces the older [[Variants of the M113 armored personnel carrier#Canada|MTVR]].<ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 20" /><ref name="Janes Land Warfare Wheeled 22" /><ref name="Canada.ca ACSV" /><ref name="LAV 6 GDLSC" />

=== LAV 6.0 Mk2 ===
The vehicle was presented in May 2025 during CANSEC 2025, a defence exhibition in Ottawa. It has a new turret equipped with a [[Mk44 Bushmaster II|30mm Mk44 Bushmaster II]], loitering munitions and two [[BGM-71 TOW|TOW ATGM launchers]] mounted on either side.<ref>{{Cite web |title=General Dynamics Canada presents LAV 6.0 Mk II 8x8 with new turret offering greater firepower. |url=http://worlddefencenews.blogspot.com/2025/05/general-dynamics-canada-presents-lav-60.html |access-date=2025-05-30 |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Design==
{{about-distinguish-text|the new variant of the LAV 6|the German light tracked vehicle [[PMMC G5]]}}
In August 2019, the Government of Canada announced its intention to purchase up to 360 '''Armoured Combat Support Vehicles''' (ACSVs), and that negotiations with GDLS - Canada had entered the final stages. Based heavily on the LAV 6 platform, the ACSVs will replace the [[Bison (armoured personnel carrier)|Bison LAV]] and the [[M113 armoured personnel carrier]] ([[Variants of the M113 armored personnel carrier#Canada|M113A3 & MTVL]]) fleets of the Canadian Armed Forces.<ref name="pwgsc.com">{{cite web|url=https://www.tpsgc-pwgsc.gc.ca/app-acq/amd-dp/vbsc-acsv-eng.html#a2|title=Armoured Combat Support Vehicles|website=tpsgc-pwgsc.gc.ca|access-date=August 1, 2020|date=November 13, 2019|archive-date=March 9, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200309224441/https://www.tpsgc-pwgsc.gc.ca/app-acq/amd-dp/vbsc-acsv-eng.html#a2|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In September 2019, [[Public Services and Procurement Canada]] on behalf of the [[Department of National Defence (Canada)|Department of National Defence]] awarded GDLS - Canada a CAD$2 billion contract for 360 ACSVs, initial spare parts, manuals, training, and various vehicle add-on kits. The various add-on kits incorporated in the procurement include: add-on armour, mine blast and enhanced crew protection, laser warning systems, side protection and [[remote weapons station]] kits. The Department of National Defence stated that by procuring similar combat support vehicles in the CAF fleet offers the advantages of reduced training and sustainment costs, in addition to the availability of standard spare parts to fix vehicles quickly during critical operations.<ref name="army-technology.com">{{cite web |url=https://www.army-technology.com/news/canada-combat-light-armoured-vehicles/ |title=Canada to purchase 360 combat support light armoured vehicles |website=Armytechnology.com |date=2019-08-19 |access-date=2020-08-02 }}</ref>

The vehicles are expected to support a wide range of operations, including domestic [[disaster response|disaster relief]] and overseas [[peacekeeping|peacekeeping missions]]. The ACSV will be available in eight variants to provide services such as: ambulances, vehicle recovery, engineering, mobile repair, [[electronic warfare]], [[Armoured personnel carrier|troop-carrying]], and mobile [[command center|command posts]].<ref name="army-technology.com"/> Delivery of the first set of vehicles is expected in late 2020, with the last vehicles being delivered in 2025.<ref name="pwgsc.com"/>

In May 2020, [[Kongsberg Defence Systems|Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace]] announced that they had signed a contract worth [[Norwegian krone|NOK]]500 Million ([[CAD$]]73.6 Million) with GDLS - Canada for delivery of the newest generation of [[Protector (RWS)|Protector Remote Weapons Stations]] (or RWS) to the Canadian Army. The Protector RWS is to be equipped on Canada's fleet of ACSVs.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.kongsberg.com/kda/news-and-media/news-archive/2020/kongsberg-awarded-contract-to-provide-remote-weapon-stations-to-the-canadian-army-worth-500-mnok/ |title=KONGSBERG AWARDED CONTRACT TO PROVIDE REMOTE WEAPON STATIONS TO THE CANADIAN ARMY WORTH 500 MNOK |author=Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace |website=Kongsberg.com/kda|date=2020-05-25 |access-date=2020-08-01}}</ref> It was subsequently announced on June 1, 2020, that delivery of the first ACSVs was still on schedule for late 2020 and would not be delayed in spite of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.shephardmedia.com/news/landwarfareintl/premium-canadian-dnd-confirms-initial-delivery-acs/ |title=Canadian DND confirms initial delivery of the ACSV for this year |last=Pereira |first=Flavia Carmargos |website=Shepardmedia.com |publisher=Shephard Media |date=2020-06-01 |access-date=2020-08-02 }}</ref>

=== Failed bids ===

;{{flag|Australia}} (211 vehicles)
:The LAV 6.0 participated to the project ''LAND 400 Phase 2'' for the production of the successor of the ASLAV named "CRV". In July 2016, the Boxer and the Patria AMV-35 were pre-selected for a final competition. Among the other competitors were the [[VBCI]] and the Sentinel II (based on the [[Terrex ICV|Terrex 2]]).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eshel |first=Tamir |date=2016-07-28 |title=Australia Shortlists Boxer, AMV-35 for Future Combat Recce Vehicle - Defense Update |url=https://defense-update.com/20160728_land400-2.html |access-date=2024-07-03 |language=en-US}}</ref>  The German-Dutch BOXER IFV was announced as the winner in March 2018.
;{{flag|Brazil}} (98 vehicles + option for 123)
:The Brazilian land forces were looking for an assault gun. General Dynamics Canada offered the LAV-700 Assault Gun equipped with a John Cockerill 3105 turret.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jr |first=Paulo Roberto Bastos |date=2021-10-26 |title=VBC Cav - LAV 700 Assault Gun, uma opção moderna |url=https://tecnodefesa.com.br/vbc-cav-lav-700-assault-gun-uma-opcao-moderna/ |access-date=2024-12-12 |website=Tecnodefesa |language=pt-BR}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web| title=LAV 700 - Armamento de Assalto | url=https://d1a5vuhmdbnak9.cloudfront.net/defesanet/site/upload/media/9046.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241213181056/https://d1a5vuhmdbnak9.cloudfront.net/defesanet/site/upload/media/9046.pdf | archive-date=2024-12-13}}</ref> The Centauro 2 won the competition in November 2022.<ref name=":12">{{Cite web |last=Higuera |first=José |date=2022-12-01 |title=Brazilian Army chooses Italian armored vehicle Centauro II |url=https://www.defensenews.com/land/2022/12/01/brazilian-army-chooses-italian-armored-vehicle-centauro-ii/ |access-date=2024-01-27 |website=Defense News |language=en}}</ref>
;{{JAP}} (Approximately 810 vehicles)
:The LAV 6.0 participated to the project ''Next Wheeled Armored Vehicle'' under the Japanese Ministry of Defense aiming at replacing the [[Type 96 armored personnel carrier|Type 96 APC]]. It was in competition against the [[Patria AMV#Patria AMVXP|Patria AMV<sup>XP</sup>]] and a new 8×8 designed by Mitsubishi Heavy Industries.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ng |first=Jr |date=2023-09-11 |title=Patria taps on Japan Steel Works for 8x8 vehicle production in Japan |url=https://www.asianmilitaryreview.com/2023/09/patria-taps-on-japan-steel-works-for-8x8-vehicle-production-in-japan/ |access-date=2024-03-29 |website=Asian Military Review |language=en-US}}</ref> In December 2022, the Japanese Ministry of Defense awarded a contract for the AMV through Patria Japan.<ref>{{cite web |title=Japan selects Patria's AMV for Type 96 replacement programme |date=9 December 2022 |url=https://www.janes.com/defence-news/news-detail/japan-selects-patrias-amv-for-type-96-replacement-programme |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221210053150/https://www.janes.com/defence-news/news-detail/japan-selects-patrias-amv-for-type-96-replacement-programme |archive-date=2022-12-10}}</ref>
